subject.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening

question: Should Gateway adopt this pre-handshake security boundary, and must forwarded-header inconsistency and protocol-mismatch rejection remain opt-in for existing deployments?
rationale: The choice changes when shared WebSocket clients are rejected, adds three public settings, and determines whether previously accepted proxy traffic fails before authentication; code review cannot safely choose those product and security defaults.

options.title: Repair the opt-in gate
options.body: Keep pre-handshake enforcement, but inspect raw header lines and place every new rejection behind owner-approved default-off settings with compatibility proof.

options.title: Approve stricter defaults
options.body: Intentionally make selected checks unconditional, then document the changed contract and provide upgrade evidence for affected proxy deployments.

options.title: Pause for origin-policy alignment
options.body: Defer this PR until the permanent origin and proxy-security configuration shape is coordinated with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98924.

recommendation.title: Repair the opt-in gate
recommendation.body: Keep pre-handshake enforcement, but inspect raw header lines and place every new rejection behind owner-approved default-off settings with compatibility proof.

likelyOwner.reason: The discussion directly identifies this person as the requested decision owner for gate placement and configuration naming on the Gateway security boundary.
